title: Season Accuracy gets its own page
text: The live record, the accuracy charts, the calibration table and every graded pick moved from Checking the AI's work to a Season Accuracy page of their own, as the NHL's and the NFL's pages have. This page, What's Changed, was added the same day.

title: Each pick is held to a like-for-like baseline
text: A pick saved without the injury report was made by Model A without its availability term, so the drift check now holds it to that model's backtest log loss, not to the full Model A's (experiments/nba/stage65/registry.json, drift.amended_2026_11_05).

title: The drift check looks five times a season
text: Instead of testing every graded pick at every run, the check looks at 100, 200, 400, 800 and 1,200 graded picks, each at one-sided 99%, the season's 95% shared among the five looks (experiments/nba/stage65/registry.json, drift.amended_2026_11_04).

title: Models fitted only on earlier days
text: Each run now refits the models on games played strictly before the day being picked, as the backtest does. Before this, a run after the day's first games had fitted on them before picking that day's later ones. A saved pick is never rewritten, so the few picks affected stay as saved and are listed in the registration (experiments/nba/stage65/registry.json).

title: The NBA's picks go live
text: The daily run saves each game's pick before tip-off, with the price and the injury report it read at that moment, and grades it once the game is final. The forward test and its drift check were registered first, on 2026-10-09 (experiments/nba/stage65/registry.json).

title: Model A and Model B, registered and backtested
text: Model A reads three matchups between the clubs: points, efficiency and who is available. Model B adds the market. Both were registered before either was fitted (experiments/nba/stage61/registry.json) and answered once on the confirmation seasons: Model A beats the base rate, and Model B beats Model A, but Model B does worse than the market alone.
